notes: Chain for MC-1 (Scenario 1; 5-state counterexample spec/output/MC_hunt_s1_bfs.out): the workload's fs2.create(/testAppendTwice/foo) carries no LAZY_PERSIST flag and its parent has no policy, so copy-on-create leaves the file's own policy id at 0 (FSDirWriteFileOp.java:831-840); after out.close(), fs1.setStoragePolicy(/, LAZY_PERSIST) is accepted because the directory branch has no copy-on-create check (FSDirAttrOp.java:463-466); fs2.append(p) then reaches the guard at FSDirAppendOp.java:121, where INodeFile.getStoragePolicyID (INodeFile.java:592-597) resolves own id 0 through the file's current ancestors to 15, LAZY_PERSIST's id, and L122 throws UnsupportedOperationException "Cannot append to lazy persist file /testAppendTwice/foo". Mechanism INTERLEAVING is the label modeling-brief.md section 1 gives this fault model: legal namespace RPCs from another client between workload steps, serialized by the namesystem lock. No fault, clock, restart, non-default configuration or timing control is involved, and it is an ordering of whole RPCs, not a race window: every tag window the model allows after the create (close, append1, append2) fires, on either / or /testAppendTwice (spec/output/diag/char_s1_*.out), and in append2 the second append gets UnsupportedOperationException instead of the AlreadyBeingCreatedException the workload expects. Phase 4a confirmed MC-1 on pristine classes of the pinned tree 734dd8a67cd (git status clean, 0 SpeculaNNTrace references in FSDirAppendOp bytecode) with repro/test_bugMC-1_append_after_ancestor_lazy_persist.java (class SpeculaAdhocFSDirAppendOpMC1Test, a variant of the workload in the same module; runner repro/test_bugMC-1_append_after_ancestor_lazy_persist.sh; output repro/MC-1.log and repro/MC-1.stability.txt): 12 of 12 tests in all 3 suite runs, the NameNode frame at the target line, and the unmodified workload passing on the same classes. The only step the reproduction adds to the workload for this route is the counterexample's own setStoragePolicy, sent through the real RPC: it writes the ancestor's xattr and never the file's own id, and the target method is unedited. Other confirmed TargetSafe finding: MC-2 (Scenario 2: Re-parenting a non-lazy file under a LAZY_PERSIST-tagged directory by rename; 7-state counterexample spec/output/MC_hunt_s2_bfs.out; repro/test_bugMC-2_rename_under_lazy_persist.java; output repro/MC-2.log; also INTERLEAVING): rename(/testAppendTwice/foo, /foo), setStoragePolicy(/testAppendTwice, LAZY_PERSIST), rename(/foo, /testAppendTwice/foo), then fs2.append throws with the same frame, 8 of 8 tests on pristine classes; the brief's rename2 OVERWRITE route (spec/output/diag/char_s2_tag_L.out) fired there too, as did a one-rename route that appends by the new path or by inode-id path, which was not model-checked because the model appends only by the workload's fixed path (spec/output/diag/char_s2_one_rename.out explores one rename at that path, with no violation). The designed route, a file created lazy-persist (MC_sanity_oracle.cfg, TestLazyPersistFiles#testAppendIsDenied), also reaches this throw, but the brief's fault model puts it outside findings and MC.tla's EnvWindow and CreateLazyFlag = FALSE keep it out of the hunts, so this verdict claims only files with own id 0 that inherit the tag after creation; char_firing_signature shows every firing in its bounded space has that signature. Phase 4a judged the behaviour a defect before any history search, from the documentation and the storage-policy contract (confirmed-bugs.md, Developer intent), and the model does not decide that question. Outside TargetSafe and not model-checked, Phase 4a also observed the truncate guard refusing such a file (FSDirTruncateOp.java:101) and the lazy-persist scrubber deleting one after a transient DataNode outage (log line FSNamesystem.java:4709; t8 to t10 in MC-1, severityProbe tests in MC-2). bounds: role 'hunt' rows are the 2 MC_hunt_* runs, each stopped at its first violation, so states and diameter are what TLC had explored by then (the full bounded spaces, from Phase 2 smoke runs without TargetSafe, are 83 distinct states at depth 8 for S1 and 13,334 at depth 11 for S2, spec/brief-coverage.md section 4); role 'characterization' rows are the 13 route runs in spec/output/diag/ (MCDiag.tla EXTENDS MC), where char_firing_signature checks FiringSignature in place of TargetSafe so the search continues past firings; seconds is TLC's 'Finished in' figure, which can differ by 1 s from the wall time in spec/bug-report.md. Left out of bounds as sanity runs, not hunts: MC.cfg (6 distinct states, all invariants hold), MC_sanity_reach.cfg, MC_sanity_oracle.cfg, and base.cfg (192,270 distinct states, structural invariants only, no TargetSafe). Model limits (spec/bug-report.md, spec/brief-coverage.md section 5): three local names, one spare directory inode, one-level mkdirs, one file with no delete or file overwrite, no snapshots, quotas, permissions or encryption zones, and appends by the workload's fixed path only. traceValidation covers the workload and 2 variants in traces/ (6, 9 and 9 events, one distinct state per event, spec/output/trace_round1/), with 209 of 209 negative controls as expected (harness/logs/negative_controls.out); those variants may not write a guard operand, so they contain no tag on an ancestor, no rename of the file and no guard=true. Those steps were checked instead by 11 fidelity probes that stop before the firing append (spec/output/probe/results.txt, all replayed through Trace.tla, with 15 of 15 mutated lines rejected in spec/output/probe/negative_controls.txt) and then by the reproductions themselves.
